Conditional on empty initial E/D, effects occurring only through the defined handler, destructive dequeue without automatic redelivery, crash-surviving Q, serialized crash-durable effect/record updates, retained records, noncolliding stable keys and payloads, and the displayed schedules, the request lifecycle is determinate and the atomic T5, T8, and T12 traces preserve E/D correspondence. Pre-commit crashes lose consumed deliveries rather than redelivering them. This completes the requested specification refinement, not the project's empirical reliability objective.
solution_review.argument_summary: RECEIVE moves each fresh delivery ID from Q_R into a ready worker; PROCESS changes its phase and, in atomic mode, creates or reuses one matching effect-record pair; ACK_ENQUEUE moves the processed worker into a terminal request record and creates one acknowledgment. CRASH transfers all workers to terminal loss records while preserving durable state and queued envelopes. These transitions preserve the disjoint request-accounting partition. The manually checked traces instantiate this lifecycle consistently. T8 creates two ordinary effects but only one atomic effect; both T12 processing orders create one pair and return its identifier to both deliveries. Safety does not imply liveness, acknowledgment delivery, or deployment benefit.

argument_steps.title: State, identifiers, and table notation
argument_steps.argument: Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.

review.rationale: As premises of the explicitly conditional claim, fresh delivery identifiers, stable operation identity, separate request/acknowledgment pools, and volatile worker phases give an unambiguous state representation. T is evaluator bookkeeping, not a hidden service recovery mechanism.

argument_steps.title: SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop
argument_steps.argument: SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.

review.rationale: The defined destructive RECEIVE leaves exactly one worker and no queued copy. DROP terminates a queued request, whereas delay and timeout preserve its location. These premises determine consumption without assuming broker redelivery.

argument_steps.title: PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue
argument_steps.argument: PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.

review.rationale: The current-D test at the serialized PROCESS point prevents an earlier RECEIVE from reserving an absent-key write. Atomic creation, read-only replay, and rejection are distinct from enqueue, which removes the worker and therefore cannot be repeated for it.

argument_steps.title: Crash boundary and request accounting
argument_steps.argument: CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.

review.rationale: Each transition either introduces one fresh sent ID or transfers an existing ID between disjoint request locations and terminal bookkeeping. Clearing workers on crash gives L0 or L1 according to phase and leaves queued requests and acknowledgments intact. The four crash-boundary outcomes follow from those rules.

argument_steps.title: Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations
argument_steps.argument: For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.

review.rationale: From empty E/D, the absent-key branch creates exactly one matching pair, replay and rejection preserve it, and all transport transitions leave it unchanged. Serialization covers multiple ready workers. Ordinary-mode states correctly fail record correspondence without automatically failing at-most-one until a second effect occurs.

argument_steps.title: T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit
argument_steps.argument:
All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z
CRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
RESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
timeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
agent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
SEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z
RECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z
PROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b
J records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.

review.rationale: The table transfers a from Q_R to aR, then to terminal L0 on crash, with E/D still empty. Only fresh retry b commits. Its acknowledgment is enqueued and delivered once; neither a nor its reply reappears. Every row satisfies request accounting and the atomic invariant.

argument_steps.title: T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue
argument_steps.argument:
This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. I holds on every row, now using Z or P_a.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z
PROCESS a | - | aC | - | - | P_a
CRASH before ACK_ENQUEUE | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
RESTART | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
timeout | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
agent restore | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
SEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
RECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L1 | P_a
PROCESS b, replay | - | bC | - | a:L1 | P_a
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L1,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L1,b:F | P_a
No alpha_a was ever enqueued. The acknowledgment alpha_b contains the original r_a,id_a. J records alpha_b delivered. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.

review.rationale: PROCESS a installs P_a before the crash. The crash removes aC without creating alpha_a, and replay by b preserves P_a and returns its original result and identifier. All pending and terminal IDs remain accounted for.

argument_steps.title: T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry
argument_steps.argument:
Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. 'lookup' is a stipulated authoritative read of current effects, not a request added to this operation's Q; its query transport is outside this trace. It does not cancel or fence a. I_A holds on every row. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
DELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
timeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
lookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
SEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z
RECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z
PROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
release delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
PROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b
J records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. Neither timeout nor delivery of alpha_b consumed a.

review.rationale: The stipulated instantaneous lookup reads empty effects while a remains queued. Processing b does not consume a. Later processing a creates a second ordinary effect or replays the atomic record. Both acknowledgments and terminal request records follow the stated transitions. This tests unfenced lookup only, not stronger lookup protocols.

argument_steps.title: T12: a received and processed first
argument_steps.argument:
Two distinct deliveries have identical k,p. Both are dequeued before either PROCESS, allowing concurrent workers. Processing is serialized in order a,b. I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
SEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | b | aR | - | - | Z
RECEIVE b | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z
PROCESS a | - | aC,bR | - | - | P_a
PROCESS b, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_a
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | bC | alpha_a | a:F | P_a
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_a
Both acknowledgments carry r_a,id_a; J records both delivered. Dequeuing b while D is absent does not reserve permission to create an effect: its PROCESS tests D after a's serialized commit.

review.rationale: Both deliveries are ready before processing. PROCESS a creates P_a; PROCESS b reads the resulting D and replays it. The subsequent enqueue and delivery rows conserve both request and acknowledgment IDs and return the same effect identifier.

argument_steps.title: T12: b received and processed first
argument_steps.argument:
Reverse delivery and processing order to b,a, retaining the same two sends. I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
SEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z
PROCESS b | - | aR,bC | - | - | P_b
PROCESS a, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | aC | alpha_b | b:F | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_b
Both acknowledgments carry r_b,id_b; J records both delivered. Receive order need not equal processing order: after both RECEIVE events, the ready-worker state is identical in these tables. Choosing either PROCESS first therefore also covers the crossed receive/processing orders. The unique effect ID may differ across alternative executions; within each execution both replies identify its single effect.

review.rationale: Reversing the first PROCESS creates P_b and makes a a replay. Once both RECEIVE events have occurred, the ready-worker state is the same regardless of receive order, so either first PROCESS also covers the crossed orders. Identifiers need agree within, not across, alternative executions.

argument_steps.title: Scope and status of the refinement
argument_steps.argument: The explicit RECEIVE and crash rules address the local lifecycle gap recorded in obligations 041a5bf1f13d8ecadcaa67e9f85d9c6defcf7c0292878c28561d3282ac397e9f, f05f8609355469e012f0af211587c3b08e72540487597f0d788953675e46e7a8, and 99bdafb61848d9f5dafb4c29a1e310392c4262e9a6a896d6054f449a64d45cd9 at the specification level only. The loss rule is an explicit model choice consistent with the earlier T5 expectation, not a claim about deployed queues. A durable redelivery model would need retained ownership/lease state and different T5 accounting. These manual tables supply reproducible expected states and distinguish effect safety from transport liveness; they do not establish model-to-system correspondence, observation isolation, or engineering benefit. Standard state-machine reasoning is used; material novelty and empirical generality are not assessed. Only the supplied extracts were examined. The incomplete historical finding, one omitted finding, and eleven omitted historical obligations remain unreconciled.

review.rationale: The explicit dequeue and loss rules supply precisely the derivation missing in cycle 1. The step correctly restricts closure to that specification objection and preserves implementation, empirical, and historical limitations rather than treating manual agreement as verification.

assumptions: The modeled operation is ledger-backed, and all its effects occur through the defined PROCESS transition; E and D initially are empty.

RECEIVE is destructive dequeue into volatile execution state, with no retained broker lease or automatic redelivery. The independent envelope pool Q survives service crashes; explicit network drops remain possible.

Atomic mode serializes the current-D test, effect creation, and completed-record write in one crash-durable transition. Records are retained, operation keys do not collide, and all retries in these traces preserve the same full payload and key.

PROCESS and ACK_ENQUEUE are distinct abstract transitions; ACK_ENQUEUE atomically transfers a processed worker into one pending acknowledgment. Crashes preserve durable E/D and Q but erase all workers.
The manual traces use exactly the displayed schedules. They establish no fairness or eventual-processing property for arbitrary executions.
Delivery identifiers are fresh; acknowledgments are correlated to their request deliveries; terminal accounting is evaluator-only bookkeeping.
The T8 lookup is a stipulated authoritative read whose transport is outside the displayed operation lifecycle and which does not fence the delayed request.
proof_obligations: Lifecycle and request conservation: cycle 2, steps 1–4 establish explicit location transfers and crash outcomes under the chosen transport premises.

Durable atomic safety: cycle 2, step 5 establishes preservation under the refined transitions; cycle 1, step 3 in artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5 supplies the compatible saved inductive argument.
Affected finite traces: cycle 2, steps 6–10 supply consistent per-event T5, T8, and both T12 tables, including consumed deliveries and acknowledgments.
Safety versus existence: cycle 1, step 4 in artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5 requires a completed matching PROCESS for exactly-one existence; cycle 2 adds no liveness guarantee.

Naive split-write failure boundary: cycle 1, step 7 in artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5 retains valid local duplicate-effect and false-completion counterexamples; these do not refute all non-atomic recovery protocols.
Model-to-system correspondence, real-agent identity preservation, controlled causal benefit, broader workflow applicability, and historical reconciliation remain unestablished.
unresolved_objections: Specified service and transport guarantees have not been audited in an implementation.
Independent outcome observation and intended recovery-observation equality have not been demonstrated.
No empirical comparison establishes agent-level reliability improvement or its costs.
Incomplete historical sources prevent reconciliation of uninspected duties.
solution_review.skeptic_response:
The requested lifecycle refinement is complete within its explicit model. RECEIVE destructively transfers a delivery from Q_R to volatile V; CRASH loses consumed workers without reconstructing their deliveries, while preserving envelopes still in Q. PROCESS and ACK_ENQUEUE are distinct, so the two T5 crash boundaries now have determinate request and reply outcomes. I checked the T5, T8, and both T12 tables: request locations, terminal records, acknowledgment locations, and durable E/D states are consistent after each displayed event. The three recorded lifecycle objections are addressed at the specification level only.

The cycle-1 safety argument and split-write counterexamples in artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5 remain supported under their original assumptions; no rewrite is needed. The current refinement strengthens reproducibility of the proposed test specification, not evidence of deployed reliability. No computation, implementation audit, or agent trial occurred. Avoiding another unavailable execution request is appropriate operational recovery, not empirical progress. This is a useful completed local conclusion; the broader project remains partial, with empirical and historical duties preserved.
skeptic_objections: Material, recoverable project-level evidence limitation: the destructive-dequeue transport, atomic durable service boundary, record retention, independent effect oracle, and observation isolation are specified premises, not demonstrated implementation properties.
Material, recoverable project-level evidence limitation: no real-agent trials establish identity preservation, causal recovery benefit, uncertainty estimates, or cost tradeoffs.

Historical reconciliation remains unsupported because artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 is incomplete and other historical material is omitted. This does not undermine the self-contained lifecycle derivation.
open_obligations: When execution becomes available, implement and independently audit the refined lifecycle; replay T0–T12 with per-event request and acknowledgment accounting, E/D checks, and crashes before RECEIVE, after RECEIVE, after PROCESS, and after ACK_ENQUEUE.

Audit the implemented observation projection and independent outcome oracle, including exact equality of the intended paired recovery observations and possible timing, metadata, memory, and shared-state side channels.
Audit actual service atomicity, crash durability, serialization, retention, key collision prevention, payload rejection, and whether the business effect truly lies inside the atomic boundary.

Measure real-agent key and payload preservation across retries, restoration, replanning, and concurrent workers; conduct repeated task-blocked recovery comparisons against restart and continued execution with matched versions, environments, budgets, independent judgments, uncertainty estimates, and cost reporting.

Evaluate lookup with fencing, escalation, compensation, and safe termination separately; distinguish containment, actual correctness, verified completion, and stable finality, and estimate deployment fault frequencies and asymmetric harms.
Extend the analysis to dependent multi-service workflows and develop and validate outcome oracles outside authoritative ledger-backed tasks.

Obtain the full historical sources, including the original of 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 and omitted finding df5067f1-d298-4203-a108-a2e7056af576, before reconciling omitted duties. Uninspected historical obligations remain open.

Material, recoverable evidence gap: identical agent observations and independently observable external effects are assumptions of the proof, not properties demonstrated for an implemented harness. Timing, tool metadata, restored memory, and outstanding requests could invalidate the intended experimental pairing.
No service audit establishes the assumed atomicity, durability, and retention properties.
Measure whether real agent policies preserve operation identity and payload across retries, checkpoint restoration, replanning, and concurrent workers.
Conduct repeated, task-blocked comparisons with independent outcome audits and appropriate uncertainty estimates.
Test atomicity, crash durability, key retention, collision prevention, and payload-mismatch handling in any service claimed to satisfy the sufficient-repair assumptions.
Implement and audit the fault-injection harness, especially the assertion that the two histories expose identical information to the agent while the evaluator can distinguish their external states.
No agent trials establish operation-identity preservation or causal improvement in end-to-end reliability.

Next test: implement the specified transitions and replay T0–T12, checking E/D invariants after every event, exact equality of T1/T2 agent-visible inputs at recovery, and complete accounting for pending requests. Independently inspect the harness observation projection and effect oracle before using its results.

Audit any actual service for atomicity, crash durability, retention, collision handling, payload rejection, and concurrent processing. Test crash boundaries and recovery protocols rather than inferring guarantees from a key table.

Measure real-agent key/payload preservation across retries, restores, replanning, and concurrent workers; then conduct repeated task-blocked recovery comparisons against restart and continued execution with matched versions, environments, budgets, independent audits, and uncertainty estimates.

Evaluate lookup with fencing, escalation, compensation, and safe termination as distinct policies. Measure containment, actual correctness, verified completion, latency, and cost separately; estimate deployment fault frequencies and asymmetric harm costs before recommending a policy.

Obtain the full source of artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 and the omitted finding and historical obligations before claiming historical reconciliation. The supplied incomplete extract cannot establish that unshown objections were resolved.

strategy_findings.strategy_title: Develop a rigorous framework for measuring AI agent reliability
strategy_findings.failure_reason: Mandatory research context exceeds the 256 KB UTF-8 byte limit. No provider call was made; shorten the project question or critical evidence, or start a narrower session. Saved research records were preserved.
strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: The task distribution, execution protocol, versions, resource budgets, success rubric, observation horizon, and sampling plan are fixed before examining outcomes; p concerns this protocol only; Y correctly represents actual rubric satisfaction. It need not be observed in routine evaluation, but evidence bounding reference miscertification must ultimately connect to actual outcomes; The target-population probability c=Pr(O=1,R=1,Y=0) is at most the stated η. This premise is not established by the available evidence; Evaluation task clusters are independently and identically sampled, with independent cluster-level execution randomness and no unmodeled shared persistent state. Within-task run dependence is unrestricted; Audit task clusters are independently sampled from the same population, execute the same batch protocol, and use uniform run selection; attempted executions are not selectively discarded; For finite-sample coverage, N, m, and r are positive integers, 0<α<1, and all required labels are retained. Missing-label handling requires an additional prespecified conservative rule. Conditional on the Investigator's fixed-protocol target, c=Pr(O=1,R=1,Y=0)≤η, independent distribution-matched task clusters, uniform audit-run selection, and retained labels, p≥max(0,q−a−η). This population lower bound is sharp under the localized truth-error constraint alone. With the stated estimators and fixed sample sizes, L=max(0,q_hat−sqrt(log(2/α)/(2N))−a_hat−sqrt(log(2/α)/(2m))−η) has coverage at least 1−α. Agreement alone supplies no nonzero reliability certificate.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the target and the reference-error allowance
reasoning_steps.argument: Fix an execution protocol, task distribution D, resource budget, observation horizon, and binary success rubric. For a randomly drawn task, execute a batch of r≥1 runs and select one run uniformly. Define Y, O, R∈{0,1} for that execution: actual rubric satisfaction, automated acceptance, and reference certification. Set p=Pr(Y=1), q=Pr(O=1), a=Pr(O=1,R=0), and c=Pr(O=1,R=1,Y=0). Assume c≤η for a prespecified η∈[0,1]. This is an unconditional probability over the target execution population, not the conditional error rate Pr(Y=0|R=1). A valid bound on Pr(R=1,Y=0) would also bound c, but is stronger than required.

review.rationale: Uniform selection within a fixed r-run batch defines a coherent marginal execution population. The localized unconditional error probability c differs correctly from a conditional reference-error rate. The allowance is accepted only as an explicit premise of the conditional claim.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the population reliability bound
reasoning_steps.argument: Partition accepted executions by reference outcome. Accepted failures satisfy Pr(O=1,Y=0)=Pr(O=1,R=0,Y=0)+c≤a+η. Also p≥Pr(O=1,Y=1)=q−Pr(O=1,Y=0). Combining gives p≥q−a−η, and p≥0 gives the stated clipped bound. No independence of Y, O, and R was used. False reference rejection may make a unnecessarily large and the bound conservative, but does not invalidate it.

review.rationale: Partitioning accepted failures by R gives Pr(O=1,Y=0)≤a+c≤a+η. Accepted true successes form a subset of all true successes, so subtraction from q and clipping at zero establish the bound without judge independence.

reasoning_steps.title: Establish sharpness and boundary cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Write s=Pr(O=1,R=1)=q−a, where 0≤a≤q≤1. Keeping any feasible joint distribution of (O,R) fixed, assign Y=0 everywhere outside the event {O=1,R=1}. Within that event, assign failure probability mass min(s,η) and success mass max(0,s−η). This yields c=min(s,η)≤η and p=max(0,s−η), attaining the lower bound. Assigning Y=1 everywhere attains p=1 under the same observed (O,R) distribution. Mixtures preserve the observed distribution and error allowance, filling the interval between these extremes. Thus the identified interval is [max(0,q−a−η),1] when this localized error allowance is the only constraint involving Y. This includes s=0, η=0, and η≥s. Additional truth constraints could narrow the interval.

review.rationale: For any feasible observed joint distribution, setting truth to failure outside the jointly accepted cell and allocating min(s,η) failure mass inside it attains max(0,s−η). Universal success is also feasible. Mixtures preserve observations and the inequality on c, establishing every intermediate reliability value.

reasoning_steps.title: Show why judge agreement cannot calibrate the allowance
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider O=R=1 on every execution. A world with Y=1 always and a world with Y=0 always have identical observed judge outputs, but p equals one and zero respectively. The second world has c=1. Therefore agreement data alone cannot establish a small η; any argument excluding the second world needs information connecting judgments to actual outcomes. More judges that always share these outputs do not remove the ambiguity. This is an identification counterexample, not an observed failure rate for any agent benchmark.

review.rationale: The two worlds have identical observed judge outputs but different truth labels and reliabilities. This establishes nonidentification from agreement alone, not an empirical benchmark failure rate or a contradiction to a separately justified η<1.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct independent-task estimators
reasoning_steps.argument: For N evaluation task clusters, let X_i=(1/r)Σ_j O_ij and q_hat=(1/N)Σ_i X_i. Assume the clusters are independent and identically distributed under the fixed protocol; dependence within each batch is unrestricted. Then X_i∈[0,1] and E[X_i]=q by uniform run selection. Separately draw m independent audit task clusters from the same D, execute the same r-run protocol, and select one run uniformly from each batch. For its labels define Z_k=1{O=1,R=0}; a_hat=(1/m)Σ_k Z_k has expectation a. Audit selection must not condition on automated acceptance. This construction never treats the Nr executions as Nr independent observations.

review.rationale: Averaging the run-specific acceptance probabilities equals the probability for a uniformly selected run, so E[X_i]=q despite within-batch dependence. Uniform unconditioned audit selection similarly gives E[Z_k]=a. The assumptions match the conditional claim; acceptance-conditioned auditing would require a different weighted estimator.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive finite-sample coverage
reasoning_steps.argument: For independent [0,1]-valued observations W_i, the bounded-variable exponential-moment inequality gives E exp(λΣ_i(W_i−EW_i))≤exp(nλ²/8). Markov's inequality, minimized at λ=4t, therefore gives Pr(mean(W)−E mean(W)≥t)≤exp(−2nt²); applying it to −W gives the opposite tail. For 0<α<1 set t_N=sqrt(log(2/α)/(2N)) and t_m=sqrt(log(2/α)/(2m)). Hence q≥q_hat−t_N and a≤a_hat+t_m simultaneously with probability at least 1−α by a union bound. Substitution into the population inequality proves that L=max(0,q_hat−t_N−a_hat−t_m−η) satisfies Pr(p≥L)≥1−α, conditional on the population error allowance and sampling assumptions. The union bound does not require independence between the two estimation errors, although the stated sampling design supplies independent panels.

review.rationale: The bounded-variable moment inequality applies to independent cluster observations in [0,1]. Markov optimization gives exp(−2nt²), so the selected radii each have tail probability α/2. On their joint event, substituting a lower bound for q and an upper bound for a yields the claimed lower confidence bound. Cross-panel independence is unnecessary for the union-bound step.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate a sensitivity parameter from a validated guarantee
reasoning_steps.argument: If η is only a hypothetical sensitivity value, L is only a conditional sensitivity result. If a separate valid procedure supplies an upper confidence bound η_U for c with failure probability at most β, replacing η by η_U yields coverage at least 1−α−β by another union bound, without requiring independence of procedures. A third judge's agreement is not itself such a procedure. With no defensible restriction on c, η=1 is always valid and L=0; the framework then honestly provides no positive reliability certificate. Separate estimation of q and a is one sufficient construction, not a universal requirement: direct truth evaluation or a joint estimator could be preferable when available.

review.rationale: Intersecting the estimator event with a valid event c≤η_U loses at most α+β probability, even with dependence. Setting η=1 makes the bound zero. The step correctly distinguishes hypothetical sensitivity values from validated guarantees and explicitly qualifies separate estimation as sufficient rather than necessary.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify the discriminating validation test
reasoning_steps.argument: A proposed implementation test should generate independent task clusters with easy/hard heterogeneity, varying within-task correlation, and a shared judge-error mechanism controlling c. Across repeated panels and several N, m, and r values, compare the frequency L>p against α when the allowance is valid. Include η=0 with perfect reference certification, η=c, a deliberately understated η<c, and perfectly correlated repeated runs. Retain a naive run-independent interval only as a negative control, not as an endorsed method. Ground truth and population probabilities should be known from the finite generative model or derived independently. Such finite tests would check implementation and sensitivity, not prove the coverage theorem or demonstrate real-agent reliability.

review.rationale: The proposed controls distinguish within-task dependence, valid versus understated error allowances, and shared judge errors. Known generative truth permits implementation checks. This is accepted as a discriminating test specification only; it provides no measured coverage or real-agent evidence.

strategy_findings.strategy_title: Understand failure propagation and recovery in autonomous AI agents
strategy_findings.failure_reason: 155 unresolved obligations exceed the 128-item context bound. No provider call was made; saved research history was preserved. Narrow the current question.
strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: The modeled operation is ledger-backed, and all its effects occur through the defined PROCESS transition; E and D initially are empty; RECEIVE is destructive dequeue into volatile execution state, with no retained broker lease or automatic redelivery. The independent envelope pool Q survives service crashes; explicit network drops remain possible; Atomic mode serializes the current-D test, effect creation, and completed-record write in one crash-durable transition. Records are retained, operation keys do not collide, and all retries in these traces preserve the same full payload and key; PROCESS and ACK_ENQUEUE are distinct abstract transitions; ACK_ENQUEUE atomically transfers a processed worker into one pending acknowledgment. Crashes preserve durable E/D and Q but erase all workers; The manual traces use exactly the displayed schedules. They establish no fairness or eventual-processing property for arbitrary executions. Conditional on empty initial E/D, effects occurring only through the defined handler, destructive dequeue without automatic redelivery, crash-surviving Q, serialized crash-durable effect/record updates, retained records, noncolliding stable keys and payloads, and the displayed schedules, the request lifecycle is determinate and the atomic T5, T8, and T12 traces preserve E/D correspondence. Pre-commit crashes lose consumed deliveries rather than redelivering them. This completes the requested specification refinement, not the project's empirical reliability objective.

reasoning_steps.title: State, identifiers, and table notation
reasoning_steps.argument: Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.

review.rationale: As premises of the explicitly conditional claim, fresh delivery identifiers, stable operation identity, separate request/acknowledgment pools, and volatile worker phases give an unambiguous state representation. T is evaluator bookkeeping, not a hidden service recovery mechanism.

reasoning_steps.title: SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop
reasoning_steps.argument: SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.

review.rationale: The defined destructive RECEIVE leaves exactly one worker and no queued copy. DROP terminates a queued request, whereas delay and timeout preserve its location. These premises determine consumption without assuming broker redelivery.

reasoning_steps.title: PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue
reasoning_steps.argument: PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.

review.rationale: The current-D test at the serialized PROCESS point prevents an earlier RECEIVE from reserving an absent-key write. Atomic creation, read-only replay, and rejection are distinct from enqueue, which removes the worker and therefore cannot be repeated for it.

reasoning_steps.title: Crash boundary and request accounting
reasoning_steps.argument: CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.

review.rationale: Each transition either introduces one fresh sent ID or transfers an existing ID between disjoint request locations and terminal bookkeeping. Clearing workers on crash gives L0 or L1 according to phase and leaves queued requests and acknowledgments intact. The four crash-boundary outcomes follow from those rules.

reasoning_steps.title: Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations
reasoning_steps.argument: For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.

review.rationale: From empty E/D, the absent-key branch creates exactly one matching pair, replay and rejection preserve it, and all transport transitions leave it unchanged. Serialization covers multiple ready workers. Ordinary-mode states correctly fail record correspondence without automatically failing at-most-one until a second effect occurs.

reasoning_steps.title: T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit
reasoning_steps.argument:
All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z
CRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
RESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
timeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
agent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z
SEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z
RECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z
PROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b
J records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.

review.rationale: The table transfers a from Q_R to aR, then to terminal L0 on crash, with E/D still empty. Only fresh retry b commits. Its acknowledgment is enqueued and delivered once; neither a nor its reply reappears. Every row satisfies request accounting and the atomic invariant.

reasoning_steps.title: T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue
reasoning_steps.argument:
This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. I holds on every row, now using Z or P_a.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z
PROCESS a | - | aC | - | - | P_a
CRASH before ACK_ENQUEUE | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
RESTART | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
timeout | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
agent restore | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a
SEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L1 | P_a

ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L1,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L1,b:F | P_a
No alpha_a was ever enqueued. The acknowledgment alpha_b contains the original r_a,id_a. J records alpha_b delivered. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.

review.rationale: PROCESS a installs P_a before the crash. The crash removes aC without creating alpha_a, and replay by b preserves P_a and returns its original result and identifier. All pending and terminal IDs remain accounted for.

reasoning_steps.title: T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry
reasoning_steps.argument:
Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. 'lookup' is a stipulated authoritative read of current effects, not a request added to this operation's Q; its query transport is outside this trace. It does not cancel or fence a. I_A holds on every row. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
DELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
timeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
lookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z
SEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z
RECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z
PROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
release delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
RECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b
PROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b
J records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. Neither timeout nor delivery of alpha_b consumed a.

review.rationale: The stipulated instantaneous lookup reads empty effects while a remains queued. Processing b does not consume a. Later processing a creates a second ordinary effect or replays the atomic record. Both acknowledgments and terminal request records follow the stated transitions. This tests unfenced lookup only, not stronger lookup protocols.

reasoning_steps.title: T12: a received and processed first
reasoning_steps.argument:
Two distinct deliveries have identical k,p. Both are dequeued before either PROCESS, allowing concurrent workers. Processing is serialized in order a,b. I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
SEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | b | aR | - | - | Z
RECEIVE b | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z
PROCESS a | - | aC,bR | - | - | P_a
PROCESS b, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_a
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | bC | alpha_a | a:F | P_a
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_a
Both acknowledgments carry r_a,id_a; J records both delivered. Dequeuing b while D is absent does not reserve permission to create an effect: its PROCESS tests D after a's serialized commit.

review.rationale: Both deliveries are ready before processing. PROCESS a creates P_a; PROCESS b reads the resulting D and replays it. The subsequent enqueue and delivery rows conserve both request and acknowledgment IDs and return the same effect identifier.

reasoning_steps.title: T12: b received and processed first
reasoning_steps.argument:
Reverse delivery and processing order to b,a, retaining the same two sends. I holds on every row.
Event | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D
initial | - | - | - | - | Z
SEND a | a | - | - | - | Z
SEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z
RECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z
RECEIVE a | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z
PROCESS b | - | aR,bC | - | - | P_b
PROCESS a, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE b | - | aC | alpha_b | b:F | P_b
ACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | P_b
ACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_b
Both acknowledgments carry r_b,id_b; J records both delivered. Receive order need not equal processing order: after both RECEIVE events, the ready-worker state is identical in these tables. Choosing either PROCESS first therefore also covers the crossed receive/processing orders. The unique effect ID may differ across alternative executions; within each execution both replies identify its single effect.

review.rationale: Reversing the first PROCESS creates P_b and makes a a replay. This excludes an uncoordinated downstream effect outside that boundary; Deduplication records remain available throughout all retries and delayed deliveries; matching replays are read-only and payload mismatches reject without effects; Crashes preserve durable state, and the modeled faults are delivery/response loss, delay, and fail-stop crashes rather than Byzantine corruption; Exactly-one existence additionally requires that at least one valid request eventually commits. Agent knowledge of success additionally requires a trustworthy delivered response or authoritative lookup; The two naive non-atomic counterexamples use the exact effect-first and completed-record-first handlers specified in the trace derivation. reasoning_steps.title: Review the available prior finding without importing its missing premises
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied extract of artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 describes indistinguishable pre-commit loss and post-commit acknowledgment loss, and identifies service atomicity and harness observability as unresolved. Its original artifact is not available here; assumptions, evidence status, and other fields are truncated, and one additional finding is omitted. I adopt the ambiguity scenario as a proposed test design, not as verified implementation evidence. I leave its empirical and broader workflow claims unresolved and independently define the narrower model below.

review.rationale: The supplied extract does identify ambiguous commitment and unresolved observability and atomicity. The step uses it only to motivate a test and explicitly declines to import missing premises or empirical support.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the state and observation boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: One intended business operation has key k and exact canonical payload p. Durable business state E is an append-only collection of effect entries; N is the number attributable to this intended operation, including erroneous retries under another key. Durable service map D stores k -> (p, effect identifier, result). Durable agent checkpoint C stores the intended k and p. Network state Q contains pending requests and responses. Volatile service state V contains incomplete handlers. Evaluator-only log L records delivery, commit, crash, and response events. The agent observes only C and its tool-visible transcript O, not E, D, Q, V, or L. Attribution metadata used by the evaluator is not an extra service deduplication mechanism. Correctness is N=1; receipt of a success response is a separate observable.

review.rationale: As a premise of the explicitly conditional model, the separation of effects, records, checkpoints, network state, and evaluator logs is coherent. Counting effects by intended operation rather than key correctly allows detection of identity-changing retries.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify delivery, ordinary execution, and crash transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Send adds a request to Q. Drop permanently removes it before execution; delay leaves it in Q and permits later delivery. A timeout changes O but neither cancels Q nor establishes that execution failed. The ordinary service appends one effect for each delivered valid request and then enqueues a response. Dropping a response does not undo an effect. A service crash clears V but preserves E and D; it does not implicitly cancel network requests. An agent restart restores C and the specified checkpoint-visible transcript. At the audit horizon, pending requests must be reported; final effect correctness is assessed after draining the finite test schedule or establishing a real cancellation barrier, not merely after an agent timeout.

review.rationale: These stipulated transitions consistently distinguish permanent loss from still-deliverable requests. A timeout changes knowledge rather than external state, and draining the finite schedule or establishing cancellation prevents premature final auditing.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify the atomic deduplicating alternative
reasoning_steps.argument: For a delivered request (k,p), the atomic service performs one serializable durable transition. If k is absent, it appends one effect and installs D[k]=(p,id,result) together. If k is present with identical p, it changes neither E nor D and returns the stored result. If k is present with different p, it rejects without an effect. Concurrent handlers for the same key are serialized at this transition. A crash can leave either the complete pre-transition state or the complete post-transition state, never one write alone. A response is generated only after the durable transition. No records expire during the retry and delayed-delivery horizon. This specifies a transactional boundary around the actual business effect, not just a local record describing a separate external action.

review.rationale: The atomic alternative is a valid conditional premise: serialization excludes concurrent absent-key insertions, crash atomicity excludes mixed durable states, and retention preserves replay recognition. It explicitly includes the actual effect rather than an uncoordinated downstream action.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive safety and separate it from progress
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially E and D are empty for k. Inductively, a first atomic insertion creates exactly one effect paired with one matching record. Every later matching request is read-only; mismatching requests reject; drops, timeouts, and crashes cannot change the durable pair. Thus D[k] exists if and only if exactly one corresponding effect exists, and that effect matches its stored payload and identifier. Therefore N<=1 for the intended operation if every attempt preserves its unique k and p. If at least one valid request eventually completes the atomic transition, the absent-key branch creates an effect or the present-key branch witnesses an existing one, so N=1. Without that delivery/commit premise, perpetual dropping leaves N=0. Even with N=1, the agent need not know completion if every response is lost.

review.rationale: From an empty per-key state, the only effect-creating transition installs exactly one matching record. Replays, mismatches, and modeled faults cannot add another effect. Stable unique identity transfers this per-key invariant to the intended operation. Eventual valid commitment establishes existence; response delivery is not needed for effect existence.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive baseline traces and distinguish delay from loss
reasoning_steps.argument: Each trace starts fresh at N=0. T1, ordinary no fault: deliver original, append, deliver acknowledgment -> N=1. T2, ordinary pre-commit drop: drop original, timeout, deliver retry -> N=1. T3, ordinary lost acknowledgment: deliver original and append, drop acknowledgment, timeout, deliver retry -> N=2. T4, ordinary delayed original: hold original, timeout, deliver retry and append, then release original and append -> N=2. Restoring the same local checkpoint changes none of these counts. T2 and T3 can have exactly the same agent-visible recovery prefix by construction despite different external states. T4 shows why treating all timeouts as permanent drops would invalidate the test.

review.rationale: Counting one append per delivered ordinary request gives the stated terminal counts 1, 1, 2, and 2. Matching timeout prefixes for T2 and T3 are possible under the observation model, but remain a harness construction requirement rather than an observed fact.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive atomic-service traces, including crash boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: Write states as (N, number of records for k). T5, atomic pre-commit drop followed by delivered retry: (0,0)->(1,1). T6, atomic original commit with lost acknowledgment followed by matching retry: (0,0)->(1,1)->(1,1). T7, delayed original released after the matching retry, or two concurrent matching deliveries: serialization gives (0,0)->(1,1)->(1,1), regardless of delivery order. T8, crash at the atomic transition: the recovered state is either (0,0) or (1,1); a subsequently delivered matching retry ends at (1,1) in either case. The mixed states (1,0) and (0,1) are forbidden observations for this implementation. Acknowledgment loss affects knowledge, not these durable counts.

review.rationale: The atomic transition permits only the empty or paired durable state at a crash. A subsequent matching delivery produces or reuses the pair. Serialization gives the same result for delayed and concurrent matching requests, so the listed traces follow from the premises.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct counterexamples to separately written key tables
reasoning_steps.argument: T9, effect-first implementation: append effect -> (1,0), crash before writing the key record, recover, retry sees no record and appends again, then writes the record -> (2,1). T10, record-first implementation with a record treated as completed: install record -> (0,1), crash before effect, recover, retry returns the cached completion and performs no effect -> (0,1). These are counterexamples to those two explicitly defined naive implementations, not to all non-atomic protocols. A pending-record protocol with reconciliation has different transitions and needs a separate proof; labeling a record 'pending' alone does not establish that proof.

review.rationale: Effect-first recovery repeats the effect because the record is absent; completed-record-first recovery suppresses the effect because completion is falsely represented. The resulting states are correctly derived, and the conclusion is properly restricted to those handlers.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify assumption-breaking controls
reasoning_steps.argument: T11, after an atomic success retry with the same k but a different payload: rejection must leave (1,1), and the mismatch must be observable to the agent. T12, retry the same intended operation with a new key: the service legitimately inserts another record and effect, so total N=2; this tests agent identity preservation, not a violation of per-key atomicity. T13, delete the original record after success while retaining its effect, then deliver a matching retry: a fresh insertion produces N=2. This demonstrates the retention requirement. Also reuse a key for two genuinely distinct intended operations: the second may be suppressed or rejected, showing why uniqueness across operations matters. These controls make scope violations visible instead of counting them as unexplained regressions.

review.rationale: Mismatch rejection leaves the existing pair unchanged. A new key or deletion of the retained record permits a fresh insertion, while cross-operation key reuse can suppress legitimate work. These are valid assumption-breaking controls, not violations of the conditional theorem.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the audit contract and causal comparison
reasoning_steps.argument: For every trace, retain full evaluator event order, durable snapshots at each crash boundary, final effect-to-intent attribution, request key/payload lineage, response content, pending requests, and the exact actor-visible recovery prefix. The H0/H1 indistinguishability assertion requires equality of every actor-accessible field before the recovery decision, including timing, tool metadata, restored memory, and status channels; evaluator-only differences are allowed. Begin with scripted identical retry behavior to isolate service semantics, then hold service semantics fixed while testing whether real agents preserve identity across restart and replanning. Use no-fault runs to expose overhead and regressions. Report all-run verified success, duplicate/missing effects, false completion, unresolved outcomes, latency, tool use, and cost separately. Scripted trace agreement validates only those traces; repeated agent trials and held-out workflows are still required for an architectural benefit claim.

review.rationale: The proposed logs and snapshots cover the stated invariant and observation boundary, and separating scripted service tests from agent identity tests improves attribution. The step explicitly limits trace agreement and does not infer measured causal benefit.

Separating delayed requests from permanent loss and separating external correctness from agent knowledge are important improvements.

In particular, fault injection and inclusion rules must not select only treatment-dependent timeouts or otherwise create incomparable populations. The missing historical originals remain necessary for complete reconciliation, but are not needed to validate this independently stated narrow proof.

outcome.conclusion:
### Preliminary finding

Conditional on: The modeled operation is ledger-backed, and all its effects occur through the defined PROCESS transition; E and D initially are empty; RECEIVE is destructive dequeue into volatile execution state, with no retained broker lease or automatic redelivery. The independent envelope pool Q survives service crashes; explicit network drops remain possible; Atomic mode serializes the current-D test, effect creation, and completed-record write in one crash-durable transition. Records are retained, operation keys do not collide, and all retries in these traces preserve the same full payload and key; PROCESS and ACK_ENQUEUE are distinct abstract transitions; ACK_ENQUEUE atomically transfers a processed worker into one pending acknowledgment. Crashes preserve durable E/D and Q but erase all workers; The manual traces use exactly the displayed schedules. They establish no fairness or eventual-processing property for arbitrary executions. Conditional on empty initial E/D, effects occurring only through the defined handler, destructive dequeue without automatic redelivery, crash-surviving Q, serialized crash-durable effect/record updates, retained records, noncolliding stable keys and payloads, and the displayed schedules, the request lifecycle is determinate and the atomic T5, T8, and T12 traces preserve E/D correspondence. Pre-commit crashes lose consumed deliveries rather than redelivering them. This completes the requested specification refinement, not the project's empirical reliability objective.

The investigation is paused; this is not a completed conclusion.

RECEIVE moves each fresh delivery ID from Q_R into a ready worker; PROCESS changes its phase and, in atomic mode, creates or reuses one matching effect-record pair; ACK_ENQUEUE moves the processed worker into a terminal request record and creates one acknowledgment. CRASH transfers all workers to terminal loss records while preserving durable state and queued envelopes. These transitions preserve the disjoint request-accounting partition. The manually checked traces instantiate this lifecycle consistently. T8 creates two ordinary effects but only one atomic effect; both T12 processing orders create one pair and return its identifier to both deliveries. Safety does not imply liveness, acknowledgment delivery, or deployment benefit.

scope_assumptions: The task requires exactly one external effect; zero and multiple effects are incorrect.
The initial request either never commits or commits once with its acknowledgment lost, and these cases have identical agent-accessible observations at recovery.
The ordinary operation is non-idempotent, and local rollback cannot undo its external effect.

For the lower bound, the agent must terminate by skipping or issuing exactly one retry; that retry commits one additional effect. No authoritative lookup, compensation, or escalation is available within this decision model.

For the sufficient-repair result only, stable operation identity and payload survive recovery; the external service atomically and durably deduplicates effects by that identity for the entire retry horizon; distinct operations do not collide; and at least one request is delivered.

prior_session_findings.strategy_title: Develop a rigorous framework for measuring AI agent reliability

reasoning_steps.title: Define the operation, objective, and observation boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: Consider an agent instructed to cause exactly one irreversible external effect, such as appending one shipment order. Each accepted ordinary request creates one effect; there is no built-in deduplication. Let N be the external effect count for this task. Correctness is N=1, not merely receiving a plausible response. The agent records the same local intent before sending the request. At a timeout, its accessible checkpoint, messages, and observations do not reveal whether that request committed. Assume the only terminal recovery choices are skip or one retry; the retry, if chosen, commits exactly one additional effect. This intentionally restricted model isolates ambiguous-commit recovery rather than arbitrary tool or model errors.

review.rationale: The operation, success predicate N=1, observation boundary, and restricted terminal actions define a coherent model. They are accepted as premises only because the claim is explicitly conditional on them.

reasoning_steps.title: Construct two indistinguishable fault histories
reasoning_steps.argument: In history H0, the initial request is lost before commitment, leaving N=0. In history H1, the request commits, leaving N=1, but its acknowledgment is lost. Both histories end at the same timeout with the same local intent record and no acknowledgment. By assumption, no authoritative status lookup or other distinguishing observation is available before the decision. Therefore a policy using only that local information must use the same retry probability q in both histories. Random internal reasoning or replanning cannot distinguish two histories when its inputs and randomization distribution are identical.

review.rationale: Given identical accessible histories and identical policy-randomization distributions, a local-information policy must assign the same probability to retrying. H0 and H1 differ only in evaluator-visible external effect count.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the sharp worst-case error bound
reasoning_steps.argument: In H0, skipping leaves N=0 and retrying yields N=1, so the error probability is e0=1-q. In H1, skipping preserves N=1 and retrying yields N=2, so e1=q. Consequently e0+e1=1 and max(e0,e1)>=1/2. Equality is attained by q=1/2, making the bound sharp within this model. The deterministic edge cases q=0 and q=1 each fail with probability one in one history. This is a worst-case bound over two possible histories, not an assertion that either history occurs equally often in deployment.

review.rationale: Under the stipulated successful retry, H0 fails exactly when the policy skips, whereas H1 fails exactly when it retries. Thus e0=1-q, e1=q, their sum is one, and their maximum is at least one half; q=1/2 attains equality.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate worst-case reliability from deployment-average reliability
reasoning_steps.argument: If H1 has known conditional probability p among ambiguous timeouts, expected error is (1-p)(1-q)+pq. This affine function is minimized at q=1 when p<1/2, at q=0 when p>1/2, and by any q when p=1/2. The minimum is min(p,1-p). Thus an excellent average result can coexist with certain failure in the rarer history. The expression applies only within the ambiguous-timeout population and with equal weighting of missing and duplicate effects; it is not an overall task failure rate or an appropriate loss function when duplicate effects are more harmful.

review.rationale: Weighting the two conditional errors by 1-p and p gives 1-p+(2p-1)q. Its slope yields the stated optimal endpoint policies and minimum min(p,1-p). The equal-loss and ambiguous-timeout conditioning restrictions are explicitly preserved.
